subject: general
question: The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s by introducing high-yielding varieties of ________.
solution:
The correct answer is__** rice and wheat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** **The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s by introducing high-yielding varieties of** rice and wheat.**
 
• **The Green Revolution in India was an initiative in the 1960s to increase agricultural production.**
 
• The high-yielding varieties of rice and wheat were** introduced during this period, which helped to increase crop yield.**
 
• These varieties were developed through cross-breeding and genetic modification to make them disease-resistant and adaptable to different soil and climatic conditions.
 
• Introducing these varieties helped reduce the dependence on imports and make India self-sufficient in food production.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Option 1: Jowar and maize are also essential cereal crops in India, but they were not the focus of the Green Revolution.
 
• Option 3: Millet and jute are mainly grown in the dry regions of India and were not the main crops targeted by the Green Revolution.
 
• Option 4: Jute and cotton are cash crops and not food crops. They were not the focus of the Green Revolution.
